cards.claim: Closed-form power-law schedules exist for momentum and batch size as functions of iteration or token budget
cards.conditions: First-order optimizers within LMO framework (normalized SGD, signSGD, Muon); holding model size fixed
cards.effect: Enables principled hyperparameter transfer across different tuning regimes and training horizons
cards.evidence: Theoretical derivation from convergence bounds in recent literature; direct claim of closed-form solutions
cards.quote: Treating bounds in recent literature as a proxy and minimizing them across different tuning regimes yields closed-form power-law schedules for learning rate, momentum, and batch size as functions of the iteration or token budget.

cards.claim: Momentum and batch-size scaling interact; optimal performance may be achieved with several scaling strategies
cards.conditions: LMO-based optimizers (including Muon); general first-order optimization setting
cards.effect: Suggests multiple valid scaling regimes exist rather than single optimal momentum-batch size combination
cards.evidence: Theoretical analysis of convergence bounds; explicit statement drawing attention to this interaction
cards.quote: Our results draw particular attention to the interaction between momentum and batch-size scaling, suggesting that optimal performance may be achieved with several scaling strategies.
